![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14187947/assets/324e3b2752fd398e47ce066dfc44f8a4d96cc3d7916f917fa142485ae86bf48f.png)

The length of a rectangular prism is decreasing at a rate of $5\,\text{cm}\text{/min},$ the width is increasing at a rate of $11\,\text{cm}\text{/min},$ and the height is decreasing at a rate of $5\,\text{cm}\text{/min}.$ How fast is the surface area increasing when the dimensions of the rectangular prism are $2\,\text{cm}$ in length, $4\,\text{cm}$ in width and $7\,\text{cm}$ in height?
question.worked_solution:
Let $x,y,z$ be the dimensions of the solid, and let $S$ be its surface area. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2\,\text{cm}, \\ y & =4\,\text{cm}, \\ z & =7\,\text{cm}, \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-5\,\text{cm}\text{/min}, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =11\,\text{cm}\text{/min}, \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =-5\,\text{cm}\text{/min}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}.$

We want to find the rate of change of $S$ knowing the rate of change of $x,$ $y$ and $z.$ So, we start with the formula for the surface area of the rectangular prism:

$$
S=2xz+2xy+2yz
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2xz+2xy+2yz) \\ \frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =(2x+2y)(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})+(2x+2z)(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})+(2z+2y)(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}).\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug in the known values into the above expression. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =(2\cdot 2+2\cdot 4)(-5)+(2\cdot 2+2\cdot 7)(11)+(2\cdot 7+2\cdot 4)(-5) \\  & =-60+198-110 \\  & =28\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\text{/min}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area of the solid is increasing at a rate of $28\,{\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{min}.$
